alignments.note: Imperative with its supplied subject pronoun; rules 7 and 9 keep 'ye' inside the verb's unit and head on the lexical verb.
Second occurrence of the adverb, aligned separately under rule 2.
The ASV supplies no second 'ye' here, so the verb stands alone; the earlier 'ye' is gapped in English and stays with the verb that licenses it under rule 27.
Comparative particle to 'as'. The supplied 'men' is not its; the anarthrous participle is what the ASV substantivizes.

Anarthrous substantival participle expanded into 'men that are'. No article stands to take the supplied nominal or relativizer, so both are rule 7 helpers on the participle itself (rule 31's test: an article would have to govern the clause, and none is present). Head on 'are', the word realizing the periphrastic future sense of μέλλω; rule 91's operational test agrees, the corpus spending 'about to' and 'are to' on this lexeme and 'men' on none, so 'men' is the generic completion rule 17 keeps the head off.

Passive infinitive with its infinitival marker under rule 61, no preposition governing the construction. Head on the lexical verb 'judged' rather than the copula (rule 17). The competing reading takes 'to' as part of μέλλοντες' own 'are to' periphrasis; I kept it with its verb because rule 61 gives the bare infinitival marker to the verb wherever no preposition governs it, and the projection's own gloss line divides the English at the same seam.
Preposition realized by the English preposition governing the phrase (rule 36).

The Greek is anarthrous, so the supplied indefinite determiner is an ordinary rule 7/51 helper on the noun it determines and no article competes for it. The packet's bracketed '[the]' in the gloss line is projection convention, not a source article.
Genitive noun rendered 'of + noun'; with no article present to anchor the case preposition, 'of' stays with the noun (rules 21 and 23) and rule 17 heads on the noun.

review_notes: Reviewed and left unchanged: all 11 source and 18 target IDs are partitioned exactly once, every unit is aligned with both heads inside their arrays, and no unrepresented or added unit is needed.

The only materially contested seam is the infinitival 'to' (t011) between μέλλοντες and κρίνεσθαι. I re-checked it and kept the accepted split: rule 7's own examples (ἀντλῆσαι → 'to draw', προσκυνεῖν → 'to worship') and rule 61's no-preposition clause give a bare infinitival marker to its own verb. The competing reading — 'are to' as one periphrasis on μέλλοντες, leaving 'be judged' to the infinitive — remains defensible and is named in the s011 note under rule 16.

'men that are' stays whole on μέλλοντες rather than being split, because no Greek article is present for rules 22, 31, 32 or 90 to operate on; the supplied nominal and relativizer are rule 7 helpers on the participle, exactly as rule 31 says of a relativizer with no article to carry it.

Head on t010 'are' rather than t008 'men' confirmed under rule 91 rather than by English syntax: the corpus spends 'about to' / 'are to' on μέλλω and never 'men', so 'men' is the generic completion rule 17 refuses as a head. This is not a case where the head is in genuine doubt.

νόμου is anarthrous, so 'a' is a rule 7 helper on the noun and rule 51's article clause does not apply; the packet gloss's bracketed '[the]' is projection convention and was not read as a source article. Likewise no article stands to anchor 'of' before ἐλευθερίας, so rule 21's bare-of prohibition keeps it on the noun under rule 23.
